components.text: The water cycle is the continuous process by which water moves between the Earth's oceans, atmosphere, and land through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.

notes.explanation: The process where water from oceans, lakes, and rivers turns into water vapor and rises into the atmosphere due to heat from the sun.
The process where water vapor cools and transforms into liquid water droplets, forming clouds in the atmosphere.
Water falling from clouds to Earth's surface in forms such as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.

components.heading: Key Stages of the Water Cycle

features.title: Evaporation
features.description: Solar energy heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers, converting it to water vapor that rises into the atmosphere.

features.title: Condensation
features.description: As water vapor rises and cools in the upper atmosphere, it condenses into tiny water droplets that form clouds.

features.title: Precipitation
features.description: Water droplets in clouds combine and become heavy enough to fall as rain, snow, or other forms of precipitation.

tiles.title: Infiltration
tiles.subtitle: Water seeps into soil and groundwater

tiles.title: Transpiration
tiles.subtitle: Plants release water vapor through leaves

objectives: Explain the role of the sun in driving the water cycle
Describe the three main stages: evaporation, condensation, and precipitation
Identify how water moves between oceans, atmosphere, and land
Understand the importance of the water cycle to Earth's climate and life

steps.label: Ocean Evaporation
steps.description: A water droplet begins in the Pacific Ocean where the sun's heat causes it to evaporate into water vapor.

steps.label: Atmospheric Rise
steps.description: The vapor rises through the troposphere, carried by air currents and wind patterns toward cooler regions.

steps.label: Cloud Formation
steps.description: As the vapor cools at higher altitudes, it condenses around microscopic dust particles, forming a cumulus cloud.

steps.label: Precipitation
steps.description: The water droplet combines with others, becomes heavy, and falls as rain over a mountain range.

steps.label: Runoff
steps.description: The rainwater flows downhill, merging with streams and rivers that carry it back toward the ocean.

components.title: Monsoon Rains: A Water Cycle in Action
components.situation: During monsoon season in South Asia, warm ocean currents heat water in the Indian Ocean. This causes rapid evaporation and the formation of massive rain clouds. These clouds are pushed inland by wind patterns, bringing heavy precipitation to coastal and inland regions.
questions: Why does monsoon season produce more rainfall than other seasons?
How does ocean temperature affect the intensity of monsoons?
components.model_answer: Monsoon season produces more rainfall because warmer ocean temperatures increase evaporation rates significantly. This creates more water vapor in the atmosphere, leading to denser clouds and heavier precipitation when conditions favor condensation over land.
